claims.text: Conventionally processed, equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi forms a homogeneous, coarse, single-phase solid solution with minimal secondary phases or precipitates.
The relatively low hardness and strength of conventionally processed CoCrFeNiTi are governed by the absence of fine grain boundaries and precipitate particles.
Fine grain boundaries and nanoscale precipitates would impede dislocation motion in CoCrFeNiTi.
Powder metallurgy or tailored additive manufacturing can promote grain refinement and/or controlled nanoscale precipitation in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Plastic deformation in the cast homogeneous solid-solution state occurs primarily through relatively unimpeded dislocation glide.
Grain refinement would strengthen CoCrFeNiTi through grain-boundary strengthening.
Fine precipitates would strengthen CoCrFeNiTi through precipitate hardening.
Increasing barriers to dislocation motion will increase the hardness and strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
Alternatively processed specimens with a refined or precipitate-containing microstructure will have higher hardness and yield strength than conventionally cast specimens of the same composition.
The predicted increase in hardness and strength may reduce plasticity and machinability.
The controlled comparison keeps the alloy composition equimolar while changing the processing route and associated cooling rate or thermal gradient.
Mechanical properties are to be compared at room temperature using standardized loading rates.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi under ambient-temperature mechanical loading.
The predicted effects require the alternative route to produce a significantly refined microstructure relative to the cast state.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant hardness and yield-strength increase, or failure to correlate any enhancement with observed refinement, would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary says the hypothesis applies in the simple solid-solution state, whereas one intervention explicitly creates precipitates and therefore may move the modified specimen outside that structural-state boundary.
